title: ilang-conformance: a deterministic conformance test set for the iLang protocol
description:
ilang-conformance tests whether a language model reachable over an API follows the iLang protocol when the specification is in its context. Every model answers the same 320 cases in three tracks (grammar 120, exec 100, judge 100), and deterministic code scores each answer with the upstream validators vendored at a pinned commit of the iLang canon (ilang-ai/ilang-spec). No model grades another model, and no score is assigned by hand. The repository ships the corpus, the case schema, the runner, the batch driver for endpoints that serve many models, the scorer, the refusal track, the vendored validators and their pin, the control-run scripts, and the per-run scores.

Version 2.0.0 (2026-09-26) pins the vendored canon to ilang-spec 4.3.0, whose wording leaves decisions to code (the model perceives, code decides). Runs made from this release on are scored against that canon and are not comparable with the runs of 18 to 20 September 2026, which were made against ilang-spec 127ba56 and remain on the scoreboard as published, with the correction of 2026-09-25 and the control runs of 25 and 26 September.

The result set: 45 scored model runs of 18 to 20 September 2026, 32 of them complete and comparable, alongside the score of every run and the manifest hash of its records. The weighted totals of the comparable runs range from 0.2074 to 0.8417, with a median of 0.5640; no run reached the L1 conformance gate. The execution track separates the field: its pass rate has a median of 0.1100 against a median of 0.8292 for grammar, and of 2,362 rule violations counted in that track, 2,205 fall on the single rule that forbids a model from signing a state declaration with an authority it does not hold.

Runs were made through two aggregator relays rather than the vendors' own APIs; model identity is what the relay returned and was not verified upstream. The scoreboard records, per run, the relay, the date, the records lost to credit exhaustion or transport errors, replies truncated before the answer, replies blocked by a content filter, one model that refused most cases under an agent persona the relay added, and five Claude runs whose replies the relay re-cased to upper case, which a second relay showed to be the relay's doing. Runs affected in that way are listed apart from the ranking. Nine control runs through openrouter.ai (pinned to the Anthropic provider), the DeepSeek and Alibaba Cloud endpoints and Alibaba Cloud's hosting of DeepSeek repeat the corpus for six models and give, per case, the agreement between routes: the noise floor of a single run, and the size of what a relay can change. Raw request and response records are kept privately; each run's manifest hash is published so a holder of the records can prove they are the ones scored. (Note of 2026-11-27: this sentence, written for version 1.0.0, has been out of date since 2026-09-27, when the raw records of all 55 runs were published with open access under DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22987356; paper/ in the repository holds the scripts that recompute every published result from them.)

Every published score is reproducible: with a run directory and its vendor entry, score.py at the commit named on the scoreboard reproduces that run's score.json byte for byte.

Version 2.2.0 (2026-09-28) adds goal-check (goal/goal_check.py), a checker for the acceptance items of an engineering book written in iLang. It is not a loop: agent tools already keep an agent working until a completion condition holds, and goal-check is what such a loop can call to decide the condition. It reads the ::RUBRIC of a book and exits with 0 only when every item passes. It has six kinds of check that code runs (status, count, json, links, file, cmd) and a seventh, human, that goes to a person. A check reads a page only when it answered 200, so an error page cannot pass a check that something is absent. The result does not rest on what the agent reports: the program reads the page, the file or the exit code itself, an item that code cannot decide waits for a person, and a confirmation signed by the agent, by itself or by a tool is not counted. An item whose premise is wrong can be disputed; its check still runs, the loop stops and the item goes to the owner of the book, and a dispute can never produce 0. It is tied to no vendor: a Python standard-library program with four exit codes that any agent can call. By default every run is recorded with a hash of the items, so a change of the acceptance between two runs shows. The corpus, the scorer and the published results are unchanged.

Version 2.2.1 (2026-11-27) corrects the instrument and changes no published score. The arm comparison of the control runs (controls/compare_arms.py) counts a judgment mode as the same in two runs only where both runs gave a schema-valid block; two replies without one used to count as agreeing. The scoreboard keeps the published agreement column and gives the corrected one beside it, recomputed from the published score.json files with no model rerun. score.py writes its generated table to report/SCOREBOARD.generated.md and no longer writes over the scoreboard, which is written by hand. cases/SCHEMA.md §3.5 describes the grammar lint file as score.py has built it since its first commit, and a test runs every golden scorer fixture. A dated note on the scoreboard says where its two refusal counts for one run come from: 238 is counted by refusal.py, and no file of the repository produces the 262 of the first scoreboard.

Version 2.2.2 (2026-11-27) corrects the documents and the checks of the instrument after the same audit and changes no published score; each correction is a dated note beside the published text. The scoreboard notes that three ranked runs (gpt-6-astra, kimi-k3 and claude-sonnet-5) were sent no temperature, as their raw records show, which left the sampling to the endpoint; that two of the nine control runs it called complete, both of qwen3.8-flash, have 4 and 8 unanswered cases; that weighted_total weighs three tracks; and that of the 32 execution failures of the first run against ilang-spec 4.3.0, 25 are wrong end states with no rule violated, not 24. report/REFUSALS.md, last generated on 2026-09-25, is generated again and has a row for each of the 55 runs; its 45 earlier rows are unchanged byte for byte. score.py writes a warning to stderr when the records of a run were sent a system message other than the one the checkout builds, as when archived records are scored after a re-pin, because spec_pin in score.json names the checkout's pin; score.json itself is unchanged. validate_cases.py gains two checks, X10 (the runtime budget quoted in an exec prompt states the case's budget object) and J10 (every boundary note re-derives with the reference function f_v5), and the 320 cases pass both. cases/SCHEMA.md names the commits its line references use and describes the request run.py sends and the record it writes. A workflow runs the bootstrap, the corpus validation, the selftests and the unit tests on every push and before a release is tagged. The suite measures the canon vendored in vendor/: since version 2.1.0 ilang-spec cad65e2 (release 4.5.1, the sealed v5.0 Pre 2.4.1); no published run has been made against it yet, and ilang-spec 5.0.0 and later are not vendored.
